parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is a single file, src/domain/entities.ts, and it covers one concern: the core domain model of a task-management app. It declares the entity shapes (User, Project, Task), the TaskStatus value set with its runtime list taskStatuses, and one domain error type, DomainError. Nothing in it belongs to an unrelated concern, and it does not bypass any abstraction of its own, since all its types work together (Task.status uses TaskStatus, and taskStatuses is typed readonly TaskStatus[]).

Two minor smells, neither enough to fail:
1. The status values are written out twice in the same file: once in the `TaskStatus` union and again in the `taskStatuses` array. The `readonly TaskStatus[]` annotation stops the array from holding invalid values, but it does not force the array to list every status. Deriving the type from a const array would keep this rule in one place. Because both copies sit side by side in one file and are type-linked, this is not real duplication across the module's boundary.
2. `DomainError` has a default `statusCode = 400`, which carries an HTTP idea into the domain error. This is a small leak in the abstraction, but it does not split the file into separate concerns.
